summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and essential tremor was admitted due to dehydration and acute kidney injury following two weeks of diarrhea and poor oral intake. She presented with elevated creatinine, hyperkalemia, and non-anion gap metabolic acidosis. IV fluids were administered, leading to improvement in renal function. Diarrhea resolved during admission, and stool studies were negative for common pathogens. Tacrolimus levels were initially elevated, prompting a dose reduction to 1 mg twice daily, with instructions to monitor levels post-discharge. CMV, viral, and parasitic studies were negative. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up on hepatitis C treatment eligibility given improved kidney function and to monitor tacrolimus levels closely.
